The US Capitol's West Front grounds: Olmsted's marble terraces and grand staircases, the sweeping West Lawn and its curving walks, Union Square with the Ulysses S. Grant Memorial and the Capitol Reflecting Pool: the foreground at the foot of the Capitol in a view along the Mall.

Scale: 0.42 blocks per metre (a storey is about 1.5 blocks: windows are single openings or slits, columns are walls or fences one block thick, roofs are stairs and slabs; keep big forms crisp and true to the real proportions, which matter more here than small detail). For a public catalog for a Minecraft 1.21.1 server: only blocks that exist in 1.21.1 (no pale oak, nothing 1.21.4+). These are real landmarks of the National Mall in Washington DC, for a hero aerial render at golden hour and dusk, seen from a few hundred blocks away and above, looking along the Mall: they must read at a glance as THESE buildings, by silhouette, colour and their one or two signature features. Build each IN SITE ORIENTATION exactly as in its map: north is low z, east is high x; the Mall runs east-west (along x), the Capitol at its east end, the Washington Monument at its west. Placement sets each module on its real footprint without turning. Exterior only: no interiors beyond what shows through glass. Light every building and landscape so no mob spawns (lanterns, hidden light sources, lit windows); at dusk the monuments are floodlit white, so put warm light at their bases. No villagers, no signs with text.

Plots along x, each standing at y 0:
 plot 0, x 0..184, z 0..124 (185 x 125), up to y 32: THE CAPITOL'S WEST FRONT GROUNDS — The Capitol building itself stands just east of this box (its west face along x 185, the box's east edge, which is NOT in the box): build up to it. From west to east: (1) THE CAPITOL REFLECTING POOL (the big water area at about x 17..63, z 14..111): a large shallow rectangular pool of still water (water one block deep over smooth stone), its edges a smooth granite coping (polished andesite / smooth stone slabs), two long sides straight; (2) UNION SQUARE and THE ULYSSES S. GRANT MEMORIAL at the pool's east end (G marks the statue at about x 63, z 77..79): a long white marble platform (about 3 blocks high, 10 long along z) with the dark bronze equestrian statue of Grant on a tall pedestal at its centre, four bronze lions around it, and at each end of the platform a dark bronze sculpture group (the cavalry charge to the north, the artillery to the south); smaller statues P (the Peace Monument side) and J (the Garfield statue) as small white pedestals with dark bronze figures; (3) THE WEST LAWN rising steadily east toward the Capitol (follow the height map), two great sweeping lawns split by a broad central walk on the axis (z about 61), each lawn edged by Olmsted's curving pale walks (Pennsylvania and Maryland Avenue walks) that arc up toward the terraces, groups of big old trees (oaks, elms: wide round crowns of dark oak and oak leaves on thick trunks) framing the lawn edges but leaving the central view open, lamp posts along the walks; (4) OLMSTED'S WEST TERRACE against the Capitol (x about 160..184): a grand white marble terrace wall two or three tiers high with balustrades, monumental double staircases climbing from the lawn to the terrace on the axis and to each side, fountains and urns, planting beds at its foot, the whole floodlit so it glows. Keep the central axis view from the pool to the Capitol completely open.

PLOT 0 (THE CAPITOL'S WEST FRONT GROUNDS): a LANDSCAPE plot, place box x 1010..1194, z 622..746. VERTICAL DATUM: module y 0 = the land's world y 4; the module replaces EVERYTHING in its box from y 1 up, so rebuild the whole ground: in every column fill solid ground (dirt under the surface, stone below) from y 1 up to the GROUND HEIGHT MAP's value, the surface block at that height, so the box's edges meet the land around it seamlessly (keep the outermost 2 blocks of every edge exactly at the mapped heights). Inside you may reshape by 1-2 blocks for terraces and steps (soften 1-block steps with slabs and stairs). Nothing may leave its plot or exceed y 32.
